messages:
sam: Quick design callout  compact scorecard row: we need alignment on undo-gesture (toast undo) vs inline confirm for single approvals. Prototype: https://files.redwood/s/compact-scorecard. Goal: freeze behavior for next release.

elaine: In tests users prefer immediate feedback + undo rather than a confirm modal. Inline confirms break scanning. Visual: one-click approve + undo toast keeps density.

jon: Impl note: optimistic update + undo requires idempotent rollback. We can do optimistic UI and send a background delete/mark call; undo will call inverse. Should be fine. Concern: frequent toasts stacking causing layout jump.

jon: Suggest toast anchored top-right with transform/opacity animation (doesn't shift content). Keep toast focusable for keyboard users.

aria: A11y points:
- Undo toast must be announced with aria-live="assertive": "Result approved. Undo." and the Undo control must be focusable via Tab.
- If we ever use inline confirm, it must trap focus and provide descriptive heading: "Confirm approve" and count if bulk.
- Ensure contrast for toast and undo button >= 4.5:1.

maya: From UXR sessions: users liked undo for single actions but wanted a lightweight confirmation for bulk approve. Recommendation: single = undo toast; bulk = confirm modal with sample rows shown.

elaine: Mocks updated: dense row with hover-revealed approve pill, toast prototype, and bulk confirm modal. I'll upload.

helper-bot: uploaded files: compact_scorecard_v1.png, toast_undo_spec.html (https://files.redwood/s/compact-scorecard)

sam: Decision summary for handoff:
1) Single-row approve: one-click optimistic update + undo toast (aria-live assertive, focusable Undo).
2) Bulk approve: modal confirm listing count + sample items, keyboard-trappable dialog.
3) Toast anchored out of flow (no layout shift) and accessible.

jon: I'll spike the optimistic flow and toast anchor. ETA tomorrow morning.

aria: I'll run a quick a11y checklist on the toast and modal once mocks are updated.

sam: Thanks all 44D. If any of you see edge cases in the spike, flag in this thread before sprint planning.
